diagnosis.root_cause: Fan motor bearing wear, supported by elevated and worsening vibration, lubricant wear-metal, and temperature signals.
diagnosis.summary: ALT-001 fired because CRAC-3 shows a high heuristic bearing-wear signal: vibration and lubricant wear-metal are elevated versus the healthy baseline, with temperature also trending upward. Recommend taking the unit out of service for approved, safe fan-bearing replacement when cooling redundancy or workload migration is confirmed; BRG-6205 is currently out of stock, so a human should approve standard or expedited procurement before maintenance.
evidence: Predictive risk is 0.776, above the 0.049 threshold.
The predictor identifies bearing_wear and cites lube wear-metal +123% versus healthy baseline and vibration +125% versus healthy baseline.
The projected remaining-life range is 23.2–31.4 hours; this is a heuristic wear-threshold projection, not validated RUL.
Recent readings show vibration and lube wear-metal rising across the sampled history, with temperature increasing as well.
BRG-6205 fan motor bearing assembly stock is 0; simulated lead time is 3 days, with a 1-day expedite option.
next_steps: Human approval: confirm N+1 cooling redundancy or migrate workloads before isolation.
Apply lockout/tagout, inspect the fan assembly, and replace the worn BRG-6205 bearing assembly when the part is available.
Re-lubricate, refit the guard, and perform the manual-recommended 30-minute vibration check against baseline before returning CRAC-3 to service.
Treat the projected remaining-life range as a heuristic and escalate the maintenance decision because the unit is already high severity.
